prompt: Put the waterfall’s phases in order.
trap: Testing comes after every line is written, which is the model’s weakness.

prompt: What did Winston Royce say, in 1970, about the sequential approach his paper drew?

choices.text: That testing should be skipped on large projects to save time for the design phase
choices.why: Nothing of the sort.
Not his point.

choices.text: That it was risky and invited failure
choices.why: Right: testing at the end is the first contact with reality.

choices.text: That it was the only correct way to build large systems
choices.why: He proposed fixes to it.

prompt: Where does the waterfall still fit, by this lesson?

choices.why: The lesson names three places.
A website can be released again in minutes.
Right: places where order and records matter more than speed.

choices.text: Start-ups that change direction every week
choices.why: The opposite: requirements change constantly there.

prompt: Inside a waterfall project, what is a tester’s best move, by this lesson?

choices.text: Refuse to sign off until the project switches to agile
choices.why: A gate, and not the tester’s decision.

choices.text: Write the code instead, so that it reaches testing sooner and with fewer defects in it
choices.why: Not the role.

choices.text: Get involved early: read requirements, write tests from them
choices.why: Right: testing can start the day code arrives.

choices.text: Wait for the testing phase, as the model says
choices.why: That is where the trouble starts.

prompt: Match each description on the V’s left side to the test level on the right that checks it.
The document a test level’s expected results come from is called its test ___.
What does the V model improve over the waterfall, and what does it not?

choices.text: It removes the sequence altogether, so testing happens alongside development
choices.why: It keeps the sequence.

choices.text: Nothing; it is the same drawing
choices.why: The pairing of levels is new.
It is the top of the right side.
Right: thinking moves earlier, running does not.

prompt: Lia writes the acceptance tests for the price rule the week Joana drafts it. Why is that prevention, in a sequential project?
hint: What surfaces when you design a test?

choices.text: Because acceptance tests replace the requirement
choices.why: They check against it; they do not replace it.

choices.text: Designing a test surfaces ambiguities before code is written
choices.why: Right: "over-60s" would have met its question that week.
There is no code to run them on.

choices.text: It is not; it is detection
choices.why: Nothing has been detected; a defect was avoided.

prompt: At which level is "`price(60, False, "thu", "20:00")` should be 1800" a test?

choices.text: Acceptance, since it checks the law
choices.why: Acceptance is the shop as users need it.
Right: one function, alone.

choices.text: Integration, because it calls a function
choices.why: One piece, nothing it talks to.
The whole shop is not involved.

prompt: At which level would the refused orders stored in the database most naturally be found?

choices.text: None: the database is not tested
choices.why: Lesson 8 tested it.
Right: each piece works alone.
The price rule is not involved.
Possible, and later than needed.

prompt: Why could the 9:30 defect only be expected at the acceptance level?

choices.why: It is a wrong price.

choices.text: Because acceptance tests run on Sundays
choices.why: Sunday was ruled out in lesson 4.

choices.text: Only there does a real session time typed by a person reach the rule
choices.why: Right: the shape of the input came from real use.
They can; nobody chose `9:30`.

prompt: In a traceability matrix, a test traces to no requirement. What does the lesson say that means?

choices.why: Asking comes before deleting.
The matrix is what showed it.
There is no requirement to cover.
Right: both are worth a question.

prompt: Which assumption do the waterfall and the V model share?

choices.why: Right: when it fails, every change is a trip back up.
Both include testing.
No.
One release, at the end.

prompt: Why is testing the phase that gets squeezed in a sequential project?
hint: The last phase before a fixed date.

choices.text: It is last, so every earlier delay comes out of its time
choices.why: Right: the phase that says whether the rest worked is the one cut.
Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Testing is optional in the model
choices.why: It is a phase.

choices.text: Because the V model moves it to the start, leaving nothing for the end of the project
choices.why: The V moves design, not running.

prompt: What does the W model add?

choices.why: That is agile, not W.
It reviews them.

choices.text: Testing in parallel with each phase
choices.why: Right: Spillner’s second V of testing.
Not the idea.

prompt: Which of these soften the sequence’s problems while keeping the sequence? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: designing tests on the way down
choices.why: Yes.
Yes.

choices.text: reviews and inspections at every phase
choices.why: Yes: static testing.

choices.text: building a small part, showing it, and building the next
choices.why: No: that abandons the sequence; it is the next lessons.
